Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 16:03:22 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry: throughput & latency needs

Hi Evelyn,

We signed up for Redwood's self-serve yesterday and flagged that we're evaluating dedicated capacity for a production rollout of our clinical summarization pipeline. I wanted to reach out directly to see if we can get a short demo focused specifically on throughput and tail-latency behavior on dedicated pools — our security team will also want to cover basic deployment isolation and audit logs.

High-level context: we're ingesting batches of patient notes and expect bursts up to ~250 concurrent requests, average prompt length ~1.2k tokens, and we need to support near-realtime responses for triage use-cases.

Can you connect us with someone who can run a throughput-capacity discussion and a live demo of a Dedicated pool? We're in PST (Seattle) and are generally available mornings next week.

Thanks,
Kai Morgan
Sr. Platform Engineer | Aurelia Health

Hi Kai — great to meet you and welcome to Redwood.

Thanks for the context — we definitely should do a short technical demo that focuses on:
- sustained throughput at your target concurrency (250 concurrent)
- 95/99/99.9p latency profiles at your typical prompt length (~1.2k tokens)
- isolation and audit/logging surface for Private/Dedicated migrations

Ben (copied) is our Solutions Engineer who runs the technical deep dives. Proposed next steps:
1) Quick 30–45m session to validate workload characteristics and show a Dedicated pool run with realistic batch sizes.
2) We'll bring a small load script and a pre-provisioned Dedicated config so you can see 95/99p latency numbers; we'll also demo KV/prefix caching behavior.

Open slots (PST):
- Mon 10/19 09:30–10:15
- Tue 10/20 10:00–10:45
- Wed 10/21 08:30–09:15

Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:05:47 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry: throughput & latency needs

Hi Evelyn — thanks for the quick reply. Mon 10/19 09:30 PST works for us.

A couple of specific asks so Ben can prepare:
- Our P99 target for the production endpoint needs to be under 120ms for single-turn summarization (we'll accept higher for longer chains but want to understand tradeoffs).
- Typical prompt size is 1.2k tokens but we also have a small % (~8%) of requests that are 4k tokens.
- We prefer an approach that avoids aggressive quantization on the critical pipeline; would like to see 16-bit/8-bit comparisons if possible.
- Security: we need to see audit logging for model invocations and an explanation of how we can access request/response logs without exposing PHI.

I've attached our capacity worksheet (aurelia_capacity_requirements.xlsx) with more numbers. Please confirm the calendar invite and any pre-demo materials we should review.

Cheers,
Kai
